Congenital absence of one thyroid lobe, usually asymptomatic. Broad hypothyroidism HPO findings do not establish common extra-thyroid damage in hemiagenesis.
Congenital fourth cranial nerve dysfunction with defining impairment of ocular alignment and motility.
Juvenile keratinization disorder affecting the skin; no common extra-cutaneous damage established.
Motor neuron degeneration; skeletal muscle wasting occurs in 80-99%. Androgen resistance with gynecomastia and sexual dysfunction occurs in 80-99%; diabetes is separate.

Mature T-cell lymphoma arising in and infiltrating intestinal epithelium; lymphoid neoplasm and lymphoma mechanism axes apply.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with developmental disability; skeletal defects and cataracts each in 2/2. Lung disease and enterocolitis each 1/2 omitted under cap.
Cranial hyperostosis and metaphyseal dysplasia define disease. Hearing loss, optic atrophy and facial palsy are reported without an established >=30% frequency.
Generalized keratinization disorder; cicatricial ectropion/lagophthalmos and limb joint contractures each occur in 30-79%. Hearing loss is very rare.
Defining eyebrow hair duplication and finger/toe syndactyly; eyebrow abnormalities do not establish ocular disease.
Uterine corpus and cervix are reproductive structures outside the axes; infection is not shared across this umbrella.
Calcium deposition directly damages the cornea and impairs vision; local calcification does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Meningiomas arise in the CNS meninges; no other syndromic organ involvement is defined.
Inherited sialic acid biosynthesis disorder causing degenerative myopathy. Hypothyroidism is separately diagnosed; cardiomyopathy is 1-4%; acquired immune myositis is distinct.
Ataxia, intellectual disability, photosensitivity and skeletal growth abnormalities define syndrome. Cardiac malformations 30-79%; strabismus and dental defects omitted under cap.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining lymphoproliferation. Hodgkin lymphoma is a separate disease; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Vertebral, carpal and tarsal fusions define skeletal dysplasia; enamel hypoplasia and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%.
Congenital enlargement of the cornea; localized ocular disorder.
D-lactate metabolism defect with elevated urinary D-lactate. Neurologic and ocular findings lack established common attribution; gout susceptibility is a separate disease risk.
Recessive IFT140 disease commonly causes retinal degeneration and renal ciliopathy. Skeletal dysplasia varies across this umbrella, which includes isolated retinal disease.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy and pes cavus reported in 1/1, with progressive muscle loss characteristic. Respiratory findings lack common frequency evidence.
